title: latency-triggered-route-ejection-journal
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal log while chasing a recurring route ejection event that looks correlated with elevated p95 token latency in region eu-west-1. This is a scratchpad — rough commands, short log extracts, hypotheses, and steps to reproduce/mitigate.

Summary of symptom:
- At ~08:12 UTC on several days, routing policy moved a subset of requests away from eu-west-1 pool to fallback pools (us-west-2, hosted) even though capacity reported as healthy.
- Trigger: p95 token latency spikes from ~40ms -> 380–600ms over ~30s. Router triggers eject heuristic then policy fallback kicks in.
- Affected traffic: production route /v1/generate for model redwood-13b-quant on dedicated-eu-west-1-1. Not all requests — seems correlated with long prefix requests (avg seq_len > 600 tokens).

Immediate notes / logs (redacted):
- Router excerpt (router-01):
  [2026-03-09T08:12:04Z] WARN route-eject: routeId=prod-gen-eu state=DEGRADED p95_tokens=582ms kvcache_miss=0.14
  [2026-03-09T08:12:04Z] DEBUG fallback-decider: prefer_burst=false fallback_target=us-west-2; policy=latency-sensitive degrade_threshold=300ms
  [2026-03-09T08:12:05Z] INFO routing-change: action=drain-target target=dedicated-eu-west-1-1 duration=45s reason=p95>threshold

- Serving runtime logs from gpu-node-07 (approx same time):
  08:11:59.342 INFO start-inference seq=4 tokens_req=720 batch_id=11233
  08:12:00.128 ERROR kernel-timeout model=redwood-13b-quant shard=0 exec_ms=312 target_ms=250
  08:12:01.401 WARN stall-detection stall_ms=470 note=attn-cache-swap
  08:12:03.009 INFO reclaim-kvcache evicted_prefixes=3

Commands I ran (local / jumpbox):
- Check recent routing decisions: curl the control plane debug endpoint (requires internal token)
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $INTERNAL" \
    "https://controlplane.internal.redwood/v1/debug/route-decisions?route=prod-gen-eu&since=2026-03-09T08:00:00Z" | jq '.'

- Pull node-level logs (kubectl to eu cluster):
  kubectl -n serving logs gpu-deploy-07 -c runtime --since=15m | egrep "ERROR|WARN|stall|kernel" -n | tail -n 50

- Snapshot model KV cache stats exposed by /metrics endpoint:
  curl -s http://gpu-deploy-07.internal:9100/metrics | egrep "kvcache|prefix_evicted|kv_hit"

- Synthetic repro (small scale):
  python tools/loadgen.py --endpoint https://eu.router.internal/v1/generate \
    --model redwood-13b-quant --concurrency 48 --sequence 650 --duration 120 \
    --auth $PROD_READ_KEY --report-interval 10s

What the data suggests (working hypotheses):
1) KV cache eviction cascade: requests with long prefixes cause repeated KV cache churn across the process group -> increased kernel exec time (more attention recompute) -> spikes p95 -> router pro-cools by ejecting the target. Evidence: reclaim-kvcache log lines and prefix_evicted metric spikes at same timestamps.
2) Kernel slower paths with quantized kernels: There seems to be intermittent switch to a slower kernel variant when memory pressure & sequence length > 512. That path adds ~200–300ms per token slice. Look for kernel selection logs.
3) Autoscaler/allocator misreporting capacity: The serving pool reported "healthy" but some GPUs moved into degraded state due to transient OOM handling and resumed but with degraded perf. Router relies on capacity health states that lag actual runtime perf.
4) Routing throttle interplay: When router drains, a sudden surge gets funneled to fallback pool which triggers local congestion and further ripples. Observed partial cascading ejections across regions.

Repro notes and minimal reproduction plan (next steps):
- Reproduce in staging with same model and long-sequence load to observe whether KV eviction alone triggers the kernel slow-path. Use artifacts from prod (same model binary + quant config).
- Steps:
  1) Deploy dedicated mini-pool in eu staging (2 nodes) with identical runtime config.
  2) Run loadgen with increasing seq_len steps: 256 -> 512 -> 650 -> 1024, each for 60s, collect /metrics and runtime logs.
  3) Capture kernel-selection trace (enable DEBUG_KERNEL_SELECT env) and kvcache tracing.
  4) If reproduced, test two mitigations: increase per-model kvcache size and enable prefix coalescing cache (experimental flag).

Temporary mitigations applied in prod (notes):
- Lowered route p95 threshold from 300ms -> 450ms at 08:16 UTC to stop aggressive ejections while we patch runtime config. (config change: routing-policy.prod-gen-eu.latency_threshold_ms = 450)
- Enabled soft-throttle on router to cap drain rate to 10% of active connections per 30s window (buy time for autoscaler).

Observed side-effects after mitigation:
- Fewer ejections across the subsequent 2 hours, but increased tail latency persisted for large-prefix requests.
- One customer reported rate-limited errors when requests stuck longer than 60s (investigating).

Open questions / unknowns to resolve:
- Does the runtime's kernel selection properly log the decision and why it chose slow-path? Need exact log keys for correlation.
- Is there a cross-talk between KV cache eviction and CUDA kernel cache invalidation that triggers extra syncs?
- How fresh is the routing control plane's health snapshot? Is there a TTL that makes router act on stale "healthy" states?
- Are there recent model changes (quantization tweak) deployed that align chronologically with first occurrence on 2025-10-29? Check model registry.

Short checklist for follow-up tasks (assignable):
- [ ] Diego: fetch full kernel-selection trace for gpu-node-07 (priority)
- [ ] Me: spin staging 2-node repro, run loadgen, attach traces
- [ ] Infra: confirm autoscaler health publish cadence and last-change timestamps for eu-west-1 pool
- [ ] Model infra: snapshot model binary + quant flags deployed on 2025-10-29 and compare to previous stable release
- [ ] SRE: consider temporary increase of fallback threshold for heavy-prefix routes until runtime fix lands

Useful snippets and config references I used while debugging:
- Router policy snippet (prod)
  {
    "route": "prod-gen-eu",
    "policy": {
      "mode": "latency-sensitive",
      "p95_threshold_ms": 300,
      "eject_rate_limit": {"percent_per_min": 50}
    }
  }
  (we changed p95_threshold_ms to 450 as temporary mitigation)

- Example kernel-selection debug env: DEBUG_KERNEL_SELECT=1 RUNTIME_LOG_LEVEL=debug

- Quick grep for kernel selection in runtime logs:
  kubectl -n serving logs gpu-deploy-07 -c runtime --since=30m | egrep "kernel-select|kernel-variant|quant-path|slow-path" -n | sed -n '1,200p'

Notes to self: keep this doc minimal and attach full artifacts in JIRA-INC-4821. If we confirm KV eviction cascade, we should evaluate a longer-term approach: smarter prefetching of KV for long prefixes, kernel fast-path stability improvements, and routing policy that considers sequence_length distribution rather than pure p95.

End of log for now.

-- Aisha K.
